top_story.headline: Army gives V2X a 24-month, $206 million sole-source bridge to run its communications in Southwest Asia, citing Operation EPIC FURY
top_story.dek: The current six-month extension of the contract ended October 31, 2026; the justification posted November 6 covers up to two more years.
paragraphs: Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground (Huachuca Division) plans a sole-source, cost-plus-fixed-fee modification for V2X Systems, LLC (formerly Vectrus Systems Corporation) to keep operating, maintaining and defending Army communications for U.S. Central Command forces in Southwest Asia. The justification puts the value at an estimated $206 million including options. The 24 months are a 12-month base period plus four three-month options. The document says the structure lets the Army end the bridge as soon as a competitive follow-on is awarded. It was posted as an Award Notice, and the attached award notice lists $211,091,828 for V2X, dated October 30, 2026, about $5.3 million above the justification's estimate.

The Army's stated reason for not competing is that V2X, the incumbent, has the unique theater footprint, host-nation business licenses, visas and pre-cleared personnel needed to avoid a break in service. According to the justification, the current six-month extension ran under Federal Acquisition Regulation clause 52.217-8 'to support critical operations through Operation EPIC FURY' and ended October 31, 2026. The justification names the requiring units as the Network Enterprise Technology Command and its 160th Theatre Signal Brigade.

sections.headline: Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board plans to buy its employees' transit benefits directly from the Washington region's transit authority, without competition
paragraphs: Eight tagged items: one sole-source justification, three solicitations and four sources-sought notices, plus one late document finding. Six of the eight are re-postings or amendments of notices listed in earlier editions; only the transit-benefit notice and a Navy Band concert-audio request are new.

blocks.title: Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board plans to buy transit-benefit administration directly from the Washington region's transit authority without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board intends to award a sole-source contract to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority for access to its SmartBenefits program, which administers transit subsidies for the Board's employees. The notice, posted as a Special Notice, relies on the simplified-acquisition rule for a single source (Federal Acquisition Regulation 13.106-1(b)) and says the transit authority is 'the sole owner, operator, and administrator of the SmartBenefits Program, the transit benefit system utilized throughout the National Capital Region.' No value is given and only the notice text was available, with no attached justification read. The pipeline logged an earlier sole-source notice for the same program from a Department of Homeland Security component.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Fish and Wildlife Service hires a local septic-tank company to drill a refuge well because outside bids ran four to five times higher
paragraphs: There were 62 new justifications today, and 36 were posted under other notice types such as Special Notices, Award Notices and Sources Sought. One is in the Washington, D.C. section and 12 are in Extensions, including the Top Story. The other 49 are here, with no repeats from earlier editions left out.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Fish and Wildlife Service hires a local septic-tank company to drill a replacement well at a Virginia refuge after outside bids ran four to five times higher
blocks.text: The well serving the headquarters of the Eastern Virginia Rivers refuge complex dates from about 1950 and is failing. The justification says contracting solicited the work twice in 2026 and six non-local companies bid roughly four to five times local estimates; local drillers had given verbal quotes of $18,000 and $25,000. It says local contractors would not register in SAM.gov because they 'consider the process too onerous,' and estimates savings of over $50,000 against the six bids. It also cites the company's 60 years in business and a well it drilled on the refuge about 11 years ago.

blocks.title: Marine Corps buys 15 Anduril secure mobile shelters for its Maritime Targeting Cell without competition, citing the company's prototype work
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Navy (Marine Corps Systems Command)
blocks.text: The sole-source delivery order goes through the existing Army single-award contract with Anduril Industries Inc. for eight Operator Shelters and seven Processing Shelters plus logistics support, to meet an urgent operational requirement. The justification says the Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory funded a 2024-2026 prototype with Anduril, and that while other vendors build standard shielded enclosures, 'only Anduril holds the proprietary technical designs' for the specific production processes. Dollar figures are redacted.

blocks.title: Missile Defense Agency gives Raytheon a 10-year sole-source task order to run and sustain its Sea-Based X-Band Radar
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The task order runs under the SHIELD contract for a 4-year base period plus two 3-year options, with cost-plus-fixed-fee and cost line items. The Missile Defense Agency says Raytheon Company, as original equipment manufacturer, has developed, operated and sustained the radar for 20 years and holds unique expertise and infrastructure. The pipeline has logged five earlier sole-source justifications for Raytheon, including an AMRAAM missile production justification listing $20,699,334,581.

blocks.title: State Department extends Africa Global Logistics' Mozambique health-supply contract without competition as management of the President's AIDS-relief program moves to the department

The justification says Africa Global Logistics has the established in-country logistics platform and that changing contractors now would risk critical health services during the handover of the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief management. The dollar amount is redacted.

sections.headline: Transportation Security Administration extends its $81 million airport baggage-screening test agreement six months after budget lapses delayed the replacement
paragraphs: Twelve new extensions or bridges today, including the V2X Systems bridge that is today's Top Story (notice). The rest are below: two federal extensions with unusual timing and a run of smaller incumbent renewals and lease extensions.

blocks.title: Transportation Security Administration extends airport baggage-screening test contractor's agreement six months after budget lapses delayed its replacement
blocks.text: The modification extends Analytical Services & Materials, Inc.'s blanket purchase agreement 70T04021A7672N003 from November 4, 2026 to May 3, 2027. The agency says the award and transition to a new contract 'have been delayed by the lapses in appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security during FY 2026.' The agreement covers integrated testing of airport checked-baggage inspection systems, with an estimated value of $81 million and about $48.4 million obligated to date. The justification calls the incumbent 'the only responsible source capable of providing uninterrupted support.'

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency Energy extends Redstone Arsenal's privatized wastewater contract 12 months, with the justification approved after award
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The contract with Mission Critical Environmental, LLC, which owns and runs the wastewater system, expires November 9, 2026, and the extension runs November 10, 2026 to November 9, 2027 with Army fiscal 2027 funds. The justification says it 'has been approved and publicized after award' under Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.103-2(d) because approving it first would have delayed the acquisition. The agency cites delays in the novation process and the complexity of the 10-year follow-on contract.

blocks.title: Air Force awards a one-year sole-source bridge to keep Platform One's Party Bus software environment running
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The bridge covers platform operations, technical and customer support, incident response, cyber security and vulnerability remediation for the Platform One Party Bus DevSecOps platform, which the justification says supports multiple Department of War mission partners. The Air Force says moving to a new vendor would require recruiting and clearing personnel and establishing access, causing 'unacceptable mission disruption.' The contract is firm-fixed-price with unlimited data rights. Two further Platform One help-desk bridge notices appear in Presolicitations.

items: Office of Personnel Management extends Excella's data-science support for personnel-record systems six months for $4,984,070 without competition. sections.headline: Army names 11 contractors to a five-year design-and-build contract for its seven government-owned ammunition plants
paragraphs: There are 313 new award notices, 39 flagged. Two multiple-award batches dominate, 11 Army ammunition-plant contracts and 10 Army Corps of Engineers architect-engineer contracts, and the rest are mostly routine.

blocks.title: Army names 11 contractors to design and build work at its seven government-owned ammunition plants under a five-year multiple-award contract
meta: Department of the Army (Army Contracting Command, Rock Island)
blocks.text: The Army Contracting Command, Rock Island awarded 11 indefinite-delivery task order contracts on November 5, 2026, with a 1,826-day base ordering period for design, build, facility modernization and commissioning at seven Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated ammunition plants. Awardees: Bering-Weston JV, LLC, Hensel Phelps Construction Co., Clark Construction Group LLC, MSM Group North America Inc., Applied Research Associates, Inc., Parsons Government Services Inc., M.C. Dean, Inc., J Kokolakis Contracting Inc., BAE Systems Ordnance Systems Inc., Alberici Constructors Inc. and Burns & McDonnell Engineering Company, Inc. Each notice posts the same $4,171,491,000, which appears to be the shared contract amount, not a per-company value.

Each notice posts $238,000,000, which appears to be a shared ceiling.

sections.headline: Army's follow-on to two big IT-services contracts carries a $50 billion ceiling and allows work in war zones
paragraphs: There are 394 new solicitations, 47 flagged, and four more flagged ones are in the White House and Washington, D.C. sections. Many flagged solicitations are re-postings or amendments of notices listed earlier and are left out unless something changed.

blocks.title: Army's follow-on to two big IT-services contracts carries a $50 billion ceiling and allows work in war zones
meta: $50 billion ceiling including optional ordering period
Department of the Army (Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground)
blocks.text: The Marketplace for Acquisition of Professional Services is a multiple-award contract that combines the Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services and Information Technology Enterprise Solutions-3 Services vehicles. According to Amendment 010, the ceiling is '$50B' including the optional ordering period, and task-order locations can be 'within CONUS and/or OCONUS locations, including warzone areas.' An industry question-and-answer file dated April 24, 2026 includes a complaint that Amendment 001 cut the recency window for qualifying projects from four years to three 'without explanation,' and Amendment 0011 added a small-business teaming track.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs' real-estate broker recompete attachments list 'Perplexity' as author and hold leftover tracked changes
blocks.text: These findings come from file metadata, not body text, in attachments posted October 16 to the Real Estate Acquisition Support Services recompete. The forecast spreadsheet's properties read 'Author: Perplexity,' an AI search tool; a Word template still holds a tracked insertion by 'Killian, Daniel S. (CFM)'; one workbook has two hidden sheets named Lookup and Data; and a lease checklist contains the path 'C:\Users\Jen\Desktop\GREX\...'. The metadata shows only what is in the files. The notice was extended to December 2 and restructured around regional networks.

blocks.title: Navy opens a rolling-admission multiple-award contract for repair and modernization of all submarines at its shipyards and refit facilities

blocks.text: Solicitation N00024-27-R-4320 gives Requirement 1, the attack-submarine framework from solicitation N00024-25-R-4321, a rolling admissions period and adds two new requirements. It covers work at the Navy's four public shipyards, the Trident Refit Facilities at Kings Bay and Bangor, Naval Submarine Base New London and Naval Base Point Loma. No value is given.

blocks.title: Army task force plans a counter-drone 'fly-away kit' prize competition
meta: Department of the Army (Southern European Task Force, Africa)
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa and the Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate are alerting industry to market research through the Army FUZE xTech Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System Prize Competition. blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency plans a five-year contract to ship hazardous waste off Diego Garcia
blocks.text: The contract would remove and dispose of regulated and non-regulated waste from U.S. military operations at Diego Garcia in the British Indian Ocean Territory. Waste would be packed into cargo transport units for shipment to the U.S. or Europe, including flammables, corrosives, toxics, batteries and automotive fluids.

blocks.title: Bureau of Prisons draft work statement for a radio network core lists Microsoft's AI assistant as the file's creator

blocks.text: The file properties of the draft statement of work for the 'Leavenworth Redundant Core' project read 'Creator: M365 Copilot' and 'CreatorTool: M365 Copilot.' sections.headline: Immigration agency adds a $4.4 million interim task order for Los Angeles detainee transportation
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

42 new awards of $2 million or more (13 are Defense Department awards just published after the 90-day hold), 10 large modifications and 6 cuts. One item tied to Washington, D.C. is in that section. The 48 routine items are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Spectrum Security Services, Inc. received $4,429,860 from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (Department of Homeland Security) on October 30 for an interim task order for Los Angeles transportation services in the Los Angeles area of responsibility, classified as security guard and patrol services. Award.

Blue Origin, LLC won a $25,380,000 task order, CX-2C, under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services contract, dated November 2. Award. Separately, Doxa Space LLC received $2,550,000 from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration on November 3 for a "Phase II brain organoids" space research project. Award.

The California Institute of Technology lost $5,000,000 on NASA's Mars Sample Return program (phases A through D) in a November 3 modification described as a supplemental agreement for work within scope. It is not a termination. Award.

General Electric Company got $2,173,363 from the Navy, signed July 30 and published this week (Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay), for rotating detonation augmentor technology for attritable unmanned air vehicles. Award.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files were approved in this window
paragraphs: During the review window from November 1, 2026, through November 6, 2026, the Office of Management and Budget approved no new apportionment files requiring special flagging, and no new or changed spend plans were identified across the 145 checked accounts.

footer.coverage_window: November 5-6, 2026 (Pacific time), afternoon edition. USAspending is pulled in the morning edition only.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments: no new apportionment files were approved in the window, and the 145 checked accounts showed no new or changed spend plans. Document coverage: 3,539 attachments on 787 notices were screened; 72 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, 49 could not be downloaded or read, and 2,756 are queued for a later edition (10,593 files overall are queued), so many flagged notices were judged from notice text alone. About 2,220 links to outside portals were not followed. Two justifications, the transit-authority and Space Development Agency notices, were judged from notice text only because no justification document was read.
